vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: memclaw
Version: 0.9.29

The 'memclaw' skill bundle is a comprehensive memory management plugin for OpenClaw that implements a tiered retrieval system (L0/L1/L2). The tools (e.g., cortex_search, cortex_add_memory, cortex_migrate) and instructions in SKILL.md are well-documented and strictly aligned with the stated purpose of enhancing agent memory. While the instructions direct the agent to prioritize this plugin over native memory, this is a functional requirement rather than a malicious prompt injection, and the security documentation explicitly states that all data processing and storage remain local to the user's machine.

llm.summary: The SKILL.md is internally consistent with a memory plugin (memclaw) and asks the agent to use plugin-provided tools, but it instructs installing an external plugin that is not bundled or verifiable here and makes unverifiable claims about local-only processing — proceed with caution and verify the plugin code/source before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name, description, and the listed tools (cortex_search, cortex_ls, cortex_get_content, etc.) align: this is clearly a memory-management plugin replacement for built-in memory and the instructions relate to that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions expect the agent to call plugin tools and to read/modify OpenClaw plugin configuration (openclaw.json) and to run migration/maintenance operations. That's within scope for a memory plugin, but the guidance to 'assist in completing configurations' gives the agent broad discretion and could cause it to attempt system config changes or read local memory files if the plugin is installed.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only and explicitly tells the user to run `openclaw plugins install @memclaw/memclaw`, but no install spec or packaged code is included for review. Installing that external package (source/registry unspecified here) will fetch and execute code outside this review — this is the main unverified risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill itself requests no environment variables or credentials. However, it expects integration with OpenClaw's configured LLM/embedding providers and may read OpenClaw config and existing native memory during migrations — meaning the plugin (once installed) will have access to whatever credentials/configs are stored in OpenClaw. The SKILL.md's claim that no external transmission occurs cannot be validated from the instruction-only bundle.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and is user-invocable. Autonomous invocation (disable-model-invocation: false) is the platform default; nothing here requests elevated persistence or cross-skill config changes beyond standard plugin configuration edits.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is coherent as documentation for a memory plugin, but the package itself is not bundled here — the SKILL.md instructs you to install @memclaw/memclaw from outside sources. Before installing: 1) Verify the plugin's source (GitHub repo/package registry) and review its code or at least its published release artifacts to confirm 'local-only' behavior; 2) Back up your openclaw.json and any native memory files; 3) Run the plugin initially in a restricted or test environment (or with limited credentials) to confirm it doesn't transmit data externally; 4) Check what OpenClaw credentials/API keys the plugin will use and ensure they are scoped and rotatable; 5) If you cannot review the plugin code, treat installation as higher risk. If you want, I can help locate the package source, summarize its repository, or list exact files to inspect for network/exfiltration behavior.
